text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT hosted-api us-east-1 queue spike. p95 gen=4.8s p99=18.4s, queue_depth=41,200, inbound RPS +580% vs baseline. Autoscaler reports repeated failures. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/ops/queues/us-east-1

maria (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm taking initial triage. First question: is this a quota/credit issue or provisioner instability? @devon please grab autoscaler/provisioner recent events and paste the tail.

devon: tailing now. seeing repeated failures: `CreateInstanceFailed: QuotaExceeded: available 12, requested 48` and `provisioner: RPC timeout to cloud provider: context deadline exceeded` around 1768801249-1768801287. Pasting small excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T16:07:29Z autoscaler: scale request +36 gpus -> failed: QuotaExceeded (limit 12)
2026-03-17T16:07:31Z provisioner: create request timed out -> retrying
2026-03-17T16:08:05Z autoscaler: backoff 30s
```

ryan: I'm going to restart the provisioner leader to clear stuck creates. Doing `systemctl restart redwood-provisioner` on leader node.

ryan: provisioner restarted. Some stuck create requests cleared and retried. However, new creates still failing with QuotaExceeded for large batch sizes.

pete: I'm going to apply an emergency edge throttle for non-critical endpoints (batching, embeddings, and long-context generation). Will shave ~35% of incoming RPS. Applying now.

pete: EDGE: `policy apply emergency_throttle_noncritical v2` -> active. Expect RPS drop in ~25s.

ash: Also enabling degraded model routing for non-enterprise customers in-region (quantized smaller-context model) to reduce per-request GPU memory. Rolling flag.

maria (oncall): Good. Two-track: (A) short-term customer facing mitigation (edge throttle + degraded models + batching), (B) infra action: request emergency quota bump and explore cross-region spill. @devon open a cloud-ops escalation for quota; @infra-lead can you evaluate cross-region capacity?

devon: cloud-ops ticket created CID-83921, requested emergency GPU quota increase from 12 -> 64. Marked high priority. ETA unknown.

infra-lead: eu-west and ap-south have spare capacity but latency sensitive customers will be impacted. We can start routing best-effort traffic to eu-west fallback pool for non-low-latency keys. Propose to shift 25% of non-enterprise traffic.

ash: Initiating routing change: fallback-route non-enterprise -> eu-west-quantized. Issuing now.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: routing rule applied, route_id=fb-2026-88.

customer-support: Drafting customer notice now: "We are experiencing elevated latency and errors in us-east-1. We have applied temporary rate limits and are routing traffic to degraded model profiles. We expect improved throughput in 20-40 minutes. We're prioritizing paid customers; contact support for impact details." Sending update to impacted list.

devon: after edge throttle and fallback routing queue_depth(us-east)=28,700, p99 down to 10.9s. Trend is downward but still elevated.

pete: enabling request-level batching for compatible generation endpoints (reduces GPU tokens). Flagging clients that may see increased latency but better success. Rolling in 60s.

maria (oncall): Incident created: INC-2026-189. Severity: Sev2. Escalating to sre-lead and infra-lead. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/hosted-queue-surge. Assigning communications to customer-support and monitoring to ash. I'm going to log a short timeline and start a post-incident doc.

sre-lead: On it. Confirming options: (1) emergency quota bump request (already opened), (2) continue cross-region spill for low-priority traffic, (3) consider temporary circuit-breaker for noisy API keys. Recommend we also blacklist a few high-volume keys identified in last 12h.

ash: Found top noisy API keys from the last 30m, proposing to throttle top 5 non-enterprise keys by 60%. Pushing denylist now.

devon: denylist applied. Early signal: further queue drop to 16.5k, p99 ~7.1s. Success rate for pinned customers improved.

infra-lead: Cloud-ops responded: can grant a soft quota bump to 40 GPUs in ~45min if we accept manual approval and billing hold. Requesting approval from finance. Meanwhile we can spin up smaller hot pools using existing quota by preferring smaller VMs (A10s) and tighter bin-packing. I'll coordinate with ryan for immediate pool creation.

ryan: creating hot-pool-small (12x A10) under current quota to absorb lower-memory quantized models. Pool creation in progress.

maria (oncall): handing monitoring and comms to ash for the next 40m. I'll remain available for escalations. Ash owns the watch and will escalate back to me if p95/p99 deteriorate or queue stops decreasing. Handoff at 1768801305.

ash: ack. Continuing watches, coordinating with infra. Next update in 10m or on change.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: NOTE: INC-2026-189 acknowledged. Handoff complete. Severity remains Sev2.
